newsitem.title: UK: Orange order has N.Ireland mayhem blueprint - paper.
newsitem.headline: Orange order has N.Ireland mayhem blueprint - paper.

text.p: Plans to bring life in Northern Ireland to a standstill have been drawn up by the Orange Order Protestant marching fraternity, the Independent newspaper said in its Thursday edition.

The paper, quoting reliable senior sources within the Order, said there would be roadblocks and other disruptions if a Protestant march in the town of Portadown, the main potential flashpoint, is prevented from passing through a Catholic district.
Earlier on Wednesday Britain invited rival Protestant and Roman Catholic groups to talks aimed at defusing fears over volatile street parades during this summer's "marching season".
The discussions will be held on Friday at Hillsborough Castle, the official residence of Northern Ireland secretary Mo Mowlam, south of Belfast, with hostile groups accommodated in separate rooms.
The Independent said the Orange Order's plan raised the spectre of a repeat of turmoil that erupted in Garvaghy Road Catholic enclave in 1996.
The Orange Order refuses direct talks with Catholic residents of the enclave, which is on the disputed marching route.

Last year the region was embroiled in chaos for some two weeks when police banned the Orange march from entering the Portadown Catholic zone but relented after four days of troubles in the province and allowed the marchers through. Catholics say that the annual procession by the staunchly pro-British Protestant "Orangemen" is offensive and anti-Irish.
Organisers say their parade is a simple celebration of religious faith and that the Catholics, who want an end to British rule, are intolerant.
